title: Incremental handoff timetable and hotlane notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notebook for the incremental handoff / hotlane approach we want to try for the next model flip (v4.1 -> v4.2). This is intentionally lightweight — a single timeline + concrete actions for the on-call/handoff window and a compact set of hotlane rules for emergency traffic and fast rollback.

Context / goals:
- Target: flip to v4.2 with minimal user impact and fast rollback if generation quality or latency regressions appear.
- Constraint: limited dedicated capacity for v4.2 during first 72h; we need to conserve quota while getting good signal.
- Primary signal: 95th/99th latency by route, quality regression rate (user-reported and eval set), token cost delta.

High-level strategy (sketch):
1) Micro-cohort warmup (0–6h): 0.1% seeded traffic to v4.2 from internal beta clients + 2 trusted customers. Observe latency and qualitative feedback.
2) Soft edge (6–24h): 1% traffic, include some anonymous public traffic via weighted routing with strict SLO checks.
3) Hotlane enable (24–48h): 5% traffic + hotlane routing for high-priority traffic (low-latency cohort).
4) Gradual decant to production (48–72h): step to 10% -> 25% if all signals green; otherwise hold and iterate.

Handoff timetable (local times in PST):
- T-12h: Final verify: model artifact in registry, checksum, and config pinning in deploy manifest (pin: model:v4.2-2024-10-01). Owner: Release Eng.
- T-4h: Preflight runbook walk-through (ops + SRE + product). Confirm monitoring dashboards and alerts. Owner: Harriet.
- T+0: Start micro-cohort warmup. Announce in #deploys and update pinned message. Owner: Evan.
- T+6h: Quick sync — 6h heatcheck (latency + sample QA). If any top-level alerts, trigger hotlane protocol. Owner: Maya.
- T+24h: Decide on moving to hotlane stage (5%). Requires green on: 95th latency per route, error rate < baseline+0.5ppt, sample QA pass rate >= 98%. Owner: Release Eng lead.
- T+72h: Final decision for next steps. Either continue ramp or roll back. Owner: Product + Release Eng.

Preflight checklist (short):
- model binary verified + checksum stored (S3).
- deployment manifest updated with pinned model tag + deploy strategy (canary window config).
- canary routing policy created: weight list, session affinity OFF for first 24h.
- observability: dashboards for per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), error budget burn, token cost per request, top prompt families.
- automatic fallback: route-level fallback to last-stable model (v4.1) with 1s graceful degrade path.
- smoke tests and golden prompts uploaded to /tests/release-golden/2024-10-01.
- contact list: SRE, Release Eng, Product, Solutions Eng oncall.

Hotlane rules (what I mean by hotlane):
- Hotlane traffic is small cohort of high-value clients (SLAs) routed to v4.2 with priority preemption. The idea is to detect critical regressions before broad ramp.
- Activation: only after 6h micro-cohort and explicit signoff.
- Limits: max 5% of total instances reserved as hotlane; cannot exceed 2x baseline concurrency per-client.
- Escalation: if hotlane p95 latency exceeds baseline p95 + 200ms or quality regression > 2ppt on golden prompts -> immediate hold + notify hotlane owner.

Rollback and escape hatches (concise):
- Soft rollback: scale down weights to 0% over 2 minutes via routing API (preferred for non-critical soft regressions).
- Fast rollback: disable v4.2 scheduling on serving pool (SRE command: servicectl disable --model v4.2) and route all traffic to v4.1. Target < 90s end-to-end.
- Production kill: if cascading errors seen, eject nodes and trigger emergency maintenance window.

Telemetry / signals (quick list):
- latency: p50/p95/p99 per route (compare v4.2 vs v4.1).
- error rate: 5xx/4xx spike per route.
- token-cost delta: avg tokens per request and compute time.
- model quality: daily eval set pass rate (golden prompts), QA sampler feedback, customer bug reports (CS tags).
- queue length and batch sizes (serving runtime metric).

Sample quick QA prompts (for eyeballing):
- prompt1: "Summarize this commit message in one line." (sensitive to hallucination)
- prompt2: "Extract the action items from this user email." (structure + extraction)
- prompt3: a targeted long-context prompt (512 tokens) to exercise KV cache performance

Roles & owners at a glance:
- Release Eng lead: Evan Zhang (deploy control, manifests)
- Release Eng ops: Harriet Lowe (coordination, preflight)
- SRE oncall: Maya Singh (infra, rollback execution)
- Product reviewer: Alex Rivera (QA signoff)

Quick commands (notes to self):
- view routing: rdctl routes list --model v4.2 --env prod
- set weight: rdctl routes set-weight --route chat --model v4.2 --weight 0.01
- emergency rollback: rdctl routes set-weight --route all --model v4.2 --weight 0 && servicectl disable --model v4.2

Known risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: noisy telemetry from low-volume cohorts (false positives). Mitigation: require >= 500 samples or corroborating 95th latency before action.
- Risk: client-side caching causing skew. Mitigation: include header override in cohorted clients to bypass cache.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we enable session affinity for hotlane clients after 24h? (Pros: stable KV cache; cons: biased latency)
- Confirm retention window for golden prompts and where to store sampling artifacts.
- Add RBAC guard on routing API for fast rollback (currently only SRE+Release Eng).

Quick timeline note to pipeline into release doc: if all green by T+72h, schedule incremental ramp to 50% over next week with daily reviews. If not green, plan a rollback and postmortem within 48h.

---
Notes to self: keep this as the single source of truth during the flip. Copy important snippets into the #deploys pinned note and the formal release checklist later.
